holidays.name: National Frappe Day
holidays.description: Today is for the frothy, ice-cold coffee drink that has fueled lazy summer afternoons for decades. Blend it, shake it, or whip it up with a handheld frother. Then sip it with the smug satisfaction of someone who has beaten the heat.
holidays.origin: The frappe was born in Greece in 1957. A Nescafé representative at a trade fair in Thessaloniki wanted a quick coffee break, but he had no hot water. He shook instant coffee with cold water and ice in a shaker, and Greek café culture adopted the result. Today's holiday is an unofficial observance that celebrates this foamy invention.
holidays.funFact: The frappe was invented by accident. It came from a worker who couldn't get hot water, and it grew into one of Greece's most iconic café drinks.

holidays.name: National Forgiveness Day
holidays.description: This is a day for letting go of grudges, whether you're apologizing for something or forgiving someone else. Think of it as spring cleaning for your emotional closet. Text the friend you've been avoiding, and finally forgive yourself for that haircut in 2014.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial observance, also known as National Forgiveness and Happiness Day. It was created in the mid-2000s and modeled on earlier forgiveness-themed days. It encourages people to reflect on how forgiveness can boost happiness and well-being.
holidays.funFact: Several forgiveness days are celebrated on different dates around the world, so you can have more than one chance each year to patch things up.
